title: The City of Glass Weather
present_summary: A coastal city in which weather is archived, traded, and enforced through civic ritual. Symbolic and linguistic resonance can alter environmental and social conditions.
core_premise: Meaning can become environment if enough resonance accumulates.

physical: Dense coastal city with mirrored towers, tram lines, salt canals, and fog bridges
Weather-sensitive architecture changes opacity depending on atmospheric pressure and public sentiment
Restricted harbor under ritual weather law
social: Weather Clerks regulate legal atmospheric release
Choir of Measures audits tonal and emotional instability
Harbor Union resists ritual weather control
metaphysical: Songs, vows, chants, and recurring phrases can produce measurable effects
High resonance can shift symbolic conditions into material or social reality

factions.name: Choir of Measures
factions.function: Auditors of tonal and emotional instability

active_tensions: Illegal weather alterations are spreading through poorer districts
The Choir suspects recent songs are bypassing normal resonance thresholds
The Harbor Union wants access to storm-release schedules
Citizens hear prior street names during fog events
Some legal weather ledgers contain unrecognized handwriting
known_transformation_scars: Some windows reflect an older skyline during damp mornings
The word 'mercy' frosts nearby glass from the inside
Tram bells sometimes ring in obsolete rhythms
immediate_story_pressure: The city is nearing a threshold event where symbolic weather control may exceed municipal containment.
